Trade Promotion Authority (TPA) and the Role of Congress in Trade Policy

For those uncertain to how the TPA is relevant to the TPP: the Trade Promotion Authority (TPA) is a piece of legislation passed by the US congress to permit President Obama to pass Trade Agreements, so long as he meets certain obligations:

"TPA defines how Congress has chosen to exercise its constitutional authority over a particular aspect of trade policy, while giving the President added leverage to negotiate trade agreements by effectively assuring U.S. trade partners that final agreements will be given timely and unamended consideration."

This is essentially to say that Congress permits the president higher levels of authority in the passing of trade agreements so long as he holds to the contingencies decided upon by the US Congress. Essentially, it makes it easier for Obama to pass the TPP.

These authorities were given by the current congress and so it should be noted which members voted for or against if they are going to use political rhetoric to their benefit. In other words, no one should be complaining about things they themselves approved.

I've been reading so much this summer, practically nonstop, and lately every time I close my eyes I end up reading to myself the next chapter of whatever book I was reading. I mean it's obviously not the actual next chapter, because at that point I wouldn't have read it yet, but it's like my mind creates a scenario for what's going to happen next and I have this internal dialogue going on in the same tone as that of the author. It's like it could be the next chapter. Do other people experience this?? Because it's freaking awesome.

I used to dream in code too. When I first learned c++, I was using it all the time and would dream about algorithms. I dreamt a program that could potentially find every prime number if it could run infinitely and I had enough memory.

I know I'm just dreaming this stuff because it's what occupies my mind during most of the day, but this makes me just love my brain.

Guys, I can't stop dreaming about writing
reading is the gateway drug to writing. A writer who don't read don't write good. Looking forward to reading your erotica!!

I completely agree. I can notice a huge difference in my writing when I go long periods of time without opening a book. But then once I read something, you can kind of see that I have learned something from that particular author about writing. It's like I start to think a little in the tone that they wrote in and it makes it makes it flow more naturally. Reading plenty of books adds more to the style.

Seriously, fearlessness is the best policy. People should - and, indeed, you'll find, for the most part, do - admire your hazarding yourself - that is putting your work out there for the world to look at and critique. Mostly, one knows if criticism is on the mark, or, conversely, is simply or complexly the product of negative motivations, like malice or jealousy - or, more benignly, simply the desire to seem knowledgeable on the/a subject.

The other, awful thing is people who really have no interest in writing at all, but are nonetheless enamoured of the idea of being a writer in much the same way as one might desire to be famous for the sake of it.

We shouldn't simply be in the business of seeking approval (we are, hopefully, no longer children thrusting a crayoned scrawl into our parents' attention), though, sadly, we do live in a world of hits and upvotes and followers.

What I want is a discerning reader. Someone who gets it, and knows and cares about style. Not someone who thinks James Patterson or FSOG are good based on nothing more or less than the units shifted.
